subject.title: [Feature Request]: Session snapshots — save and load context checkpoints (/session save|load)

question: Should OpenClaw own first-class named session snapshots/save-load, and what initial semantics should cover save/load, branch/restore, and archived transcript import?
rationale: The unresolved behavior spans durable session storage, destructive restore semantics, checkpoint retention and naming, deleted/archive privacy, Gateway protocol, slash/CLI/UI UX, and prompt-cache-sensitive forks, so code inspection cannot choose the product contract alone.

options.title: Design core snapshot contract first
options.body: Define a versioned core session snapshot/checkpoint contract that composes existing compaction checkpoints with archive recovery and then implement the first bounded slice.

options.title: Ship a narrower resume slice
options.body: Approve a read-only session/archive listing and resume path first, leaving arbitrary named save/load snapshots and templates for a later issue.

options.title: Keep only adjacent primitives
options.body: Decline first-class named snapshots for core and continue tracking only compaction checkpoint recovery, archive reindexing, and fork/resume issues separately.

recommendation.title: Design core snapshot contract first
recommendation.body: Define a versioned core session snapshot/checkpoint contract that composes existing compaction checkpoints with archive recovery and then implement the first bounded slice.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger is the clearest product/API routing owner from the issue discussion and recent session lifecycle history.
